title: Thrombolysis in patients on antithrombotics or with coagulopathy
keyNumbers: Platelets <100,000/mm³, INR >1.7, aPTT >40 s, or PT >15 s: Do not give IVT
No recent warfarin or heparin: Start IVT before coagulation results return; stop if INR >1.7 or PT/PTT is abnormal by local standards

DOAC taken <48 h, disabling deficit, within window: May be considered after individual benefit–risk review: time of last dose, renal function, severity, EVT availability, reversal agents, DOAC-specific anti-Xa or thrombin time assays. Document timing, reversal use, and assay results
Prior antiplatelet monotherapy (SAPT) or DAPT, otherwise eligible: Give IVT — sICH rises ~0.9% (SAPT) / 1.2% (DAPT) absolute vs no antiplatelet, outweighed by ~8% absolute benefit
Full treatment-dose LMWH within the previous 24 h: Do not give IVT; doesn't apply to prophylactic doses
question: Can this patient on (or recently on) an antithrombotic receive IV thrombolysis?
population: Adults with AIS otherwise eligible for IVT within the treatment window

rules.recommendation: Start IVT before coagulation results return; stop if INR >1.7 or PT/PTT is abnormal by local standards
evidenceNote: Table 8 is ungraded: expert opinion and limited data

rules.condition: Platelets <100,000/mm³, INR >1.7, aPTT >40 s, or PT >15 s
evidenceNote: AHA 2026 Table 8: safety unknown, may substantially increase harm
Table 8 is ungraded: expert opinion and limited data

rules.condition: DOAC taken <48 h, disabling deficit, within window
rules.recommendation: May be considered after individual benefit–risk review: time of last dose, renal function, severity, EVT availability, reversal agents, DOAC-specific anti-Xa or thrombin time assays. Document timing, reversal use, and assay results
evidenceNote: AHA 2026 Table 8: relative contraindication; observational data only
Several cohorts found no excess sICH with DOAC exposure, but anticoagulated patients were excluded from pivotal trials

rules.condition: Prior antiplatelet monotherapy (SAPT) or DAPT, otherwise eligible
rules.recommendation: Give IVT — sICH rises ~0.9% (SAPT) / 1.2% (DAPT) absolute vs no antiplatelet, outweighed by ~8% absolute benefit
evidenceNote: sICH and benefit figures: AHA 2026 §4.6.1 supportive text 9

rules.condition: Full treatment-dose LMWH within the previous 24 h
rules.recommendation: Do not give IVT; doesn't apply to prophylactic doses
evidenceNote: Powers 2019 §3.5.5 Rec 7: COR III: Harm, LOE B-NR
Not restated in AHA 2026 §4.6 or Table 8

rules.recommendation: Hold antiplatelets and anticoagulants until the 24-h CT/MRI
evidenceNote: Table 7 is an ungraded treatment protocol

contraindications: Acute intracranial hemorrhage or extensive clear hypodensity on CT
Intracranial/spinal surgery within 14 days; moderate–severe TBI within 14 days; spinal cord injury within 3 months
Intra-axial intracranial neoplasm; infective endocarditis; aortic arch dissection
institutionVaries: Availability of rapid drug-specific anti-Xa / thrombin-time assays
Local policy on IVT with DOAC <48 h
Local policy on LMWH exposure (AHA 2026 silent; Powers 2019 rule applies to full doses only)
pearls: Don't delay thrombectomy work-up while sorting out anticoagulant status
sources: Prabhakaran S, et al. 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2026;57:e316-e436. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000513
